item.text: South Australia’s Independent Commission Against Corruption analysed local government responses to its third Public Integrity Survey.
item.support:
It analyses the perceptions and 
experiences of public officers in the local government 
sector.

item.text: The survey focused on decision making, discretionary powers and improper influence, while comparing compatible results with earlier surveys.
item.support:
The 2024 survey focused specifically on risks relating to decision making, including 
the use of discretionary powers, and improper influence.

item.text: The Commission reported increasing perceptions of corruption vulnerability, while cautioning that greater awareness could explain the change.
item.support:
This does not necessarily 
mean that local councils are experiencing more corrupt conduct.

item.text: The Commission identified risks around recruitment favouritism, procurement, confidential information and unchecked decision making, and encouraged officers to use reporting systems.
item.support:
Decision making that lacks transparency, accountability, and 
appropriate checks and balances, may be vulnerable to misuse of authority.
